records.d: Long before writing, storytellers kept recurring characters alive across generations: tricksters, heroes, and gods who grew with each telling. The interactive character's oldest form is the tale told again, changed by its audience. Characters have always been co-created.
records.h: Bards adapted recurring figures to each audience, letting listener reactions shape the character over tellings. The story was the interface. The character lived in the telling.
records.mj: Established - documented oral tradition; recurring characters shaped by audiences.

records.d: Sherlock Holmes debuted in 1887 and became literature's first serialized character with a persistent life across stories: readers followed a person, not just plots. The character became the franchise. Fictional persons gained continuity.
records.h: Conan Doyle maintained Holmes's biography, habits, and relationships across dozens of stories, with readers tracking continuity. The character was the product. Serialization made fiction persistent.
records.mj: Established - documented 1887 debut; serialized persistent fictional character.

records.d: Dungeons & Dragons, released in 1974, let players become persistent characters with stats, memories, and growth across sessions. The character was yours and it remembered. Roleplay made fiction interactive.
records.h: Character sheets tracked abilities, inventory, and history while dungeon masters adjudicated a shared world. The character persisted between sessions. The player was the AI.
records.mj: Established - documented 1974 release; persistent player characters.

records.d: Zork, released commercially in 1980, populated its caves with characters you could talk to and trade with: the thief, the troll. Text characters with behaviors. Fiction's persons gained simple minds.
records.h: Parser-based NPCs responded to typed commands with scripted behaviors and inventories. The interaction was textual. The character was a program.
records.mj: Established - documented 1980 commercial release; interactive text NPCs.

records.d: MUDs in 1980 let players inhabit persistent characters in shared text worlds: the character lived online. Thousands roleplayed together. The fictional person gained a network.
records.h: Server-hosted text worlds maintained character state across sessions for many simultaneous players. The world persisted. The character was an online identity.
records.mj: Established - documented MUD era; persistent multiplayer characters.

records.d: Tamagotchi, launched in 1996, put a persistent digital creature in millions of pockets: it needed feeding, grew, and could die. The character needed you. Digital persons gained dependence.
records.h: A simple state machine tracked hunger, happiness, and age, with neglect leading to death. The owner was responsible. Attachment was the product.
records.mj: Established - documented 1996 Bandai launch; persistent digital pets.

records.d: Creatures, released in 1996, raised Norns with neural-network brains that learned: creatures you taught, who remembered. The pet had a mind. Game characters gained learning.
records.h: Neural networks controlled creature behavior, with reinforcement from player interaction shaping development. The Norn learned. The character was trainable.
records.mj: Established - documented 1996 release; neural-network learning creatures.

records.d: Black & White, released in 2001, gave players a giant Creature that learned from praise and punishment: a god-game character with a developing personality. The character had morals you taught. Agency met upbringing.

records.d: Nintendogs, released in 2005, put persistent puppies on the DS: voice-responsive, trainable, remembering. The handheld pet learned tricks. Portable characters deepened bonds.
records.h: Voice recognition and touch drove training, with persistent state tracking each dog's learned tricks and mood. The pet remembered. The handheld became a companion.
records.mj: Established - documented 2005 Nintendo release; persistent virtual pets.

records.d: Siri, launched in October 2011, gave millions a conversational character in their phone: a persona with humor and memory of context. The assistant had personality. Software gained a character.
records.h: Voice dialogue with scripted personality and contextual memory handled tasks conversationally. The persona was designed. The phone had a character.
records.mj: Established - documented October 2011 launch; conversational assistant persona.

records.d: Undertale, released in 2015, featured characters who remembered across playthroughs: Flowey knew what you did last run. The character remembered you. Fiction gained memory of the player.
records.h: Save-file-aware writing let characters reference previous runs, deaths, and choices. The fourth wall was load-bearing. The character's memory included the player.
records.mj: Established - documented 2015 release; characters with cross-run memory.

records.d: Westworld, premiering in 2016, dramatized hosts: artificial characters with scripted loops gaining memory and selfhood. Fiction explored the interactive character's inner life. The thought experiment went primetime.

records.mj: Established - documented 2016 HBO premiere; drama of artificial characters.

records.d: Detroit: Become Human, released in 2018, wove branching android characters whose personalities shifted with player choices across a diverging story. The character was a possibility space. Choice shaped persons.

records.mj: Established - documented 2018 release; branching character narratives.

records.d: In 2020, users discovered GPT-3 could roleplay any character convincingly: historical figures, fictional heroes, original personas. The model was a cast of thousands. Character became a prompt.
